tasks.short: Evaluate treatment effects and adjust interventions

steps.what: Evaluate treatment effects using current observations, progress and patient experience
Adjust treatments with the patient to achieve appropriate benefit

tasks.design: Retain clinical evaluation and treatment adjustment with the therapist using the clinical record {OTHER}. A trend in a measurement does not become an automatic treatment instruction; clinical observations and the patient's experience remain part of the decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Treatment response depends on symptoms, function, goals and changing circumstances.
tasks.enabler_now: Documentation tools do not establish a validated replacement for this clinical judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing meaningful response from variation and choosing an appropriate adjustment.
tasks.human_edge: The therapist notices pain, hesitation or a changed goal that a numerical trend may conceal.
tasks.altitude: Evaluation time and clinical responsibilities remain unchanged.

reach.task: Discuss a functional limitation affecting treatment goals

evidence.claim: Treatment response evaluation and adjustment require patient-specific clinical judgement; documentation capability alone establishes no labour saving.

assumptions: Boundary is evaluation and treatment adjustment, excluding measurement capture and general record maintenance.

Therapist or authorised clinical staff produce progress measurements through existing assessment work; patient supplies experience during the retained encounter. No structured treatment-response classification is assumed.
Therapist produces evaluated response in s1 before adjustment in s2. Local professional scope and patient agreement remain controlling.
Review native record presentation before future custom work. No new software or maintained process is introduced, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Treatment types and local clinical scope
research_questions: Which response uncertainties need more assessment rather than faster trend presentation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and upkeep=0. Routine and uncertain response evaluations retain interpretation and patient discussion; measurement-entry gains belong to their own task.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer with patients and clinicians about intervention programmes

steps.what: Confer with the patient and practitioners to plan, implement or assess interventions

tasks.design: Keep intervention discussion and coordination with the therapist, patient and relevant clinicians. Existing programme information can remain in the clinical record {OTHER}; this task does not add a recording or minutes-production duty.
tasks.previous_blocker: Participants hold different information and need a shared understanding of goals and responsibilities.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital records support access but do not replace the conversation or establish a shorter safe discussion.
tasks.still_hard: Resolving differing priorities, uncertainties and practical barriers to implementation.
tasks.human_edge: The therapist detects disagreement or misunderstanding and changes the explanation or plan.
tasks.altitude: Intervention discussion time and participant rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Clarify an agreed intervention responsibility with the therapist

evidence.claim: Collaborative intervention discussion needs interpretation and agreement; no distinct administrative baseline is established here.

assumptions: Boundary is therapist participation in the discussion, excluding other participants' labour and later record drafting.
Patient and clinicians produce observations and clarify goals in the retained conversation; no ready structured agreement is assumed.
Native record access should be checked before later custom work. Current access earns no new saving and no ambient recording is introduced.
No software or process is introduced, so upkeep is zero. Overlap with treatment-adjustment discussion must be allocated once in role totals.
research_questions: Are coordination delays due to missing information access or necessary goal negotiation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and upkeep=0. Straightforward and disputed interventions retain discussion time; no invented coordination report is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Obtain patients' informed consent to interventions

steps.what: Explain proposed interventions, alternatives and risks and obtain informed consent
Record the consent discussion, patient decision and any intervention limits

tasks.design: Configure a consent-record form in the clinical record {OTHER} with existing patient and encounter fields. The therapist still explains and checks understanding, then records the actual decision and its limits; a completed form never implies consent by itself.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated identity and encounter entry can duplicate information during consent documentation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native forms can reuse existing identifiers while leaving the consent outcome for the therapist to enter.
tasks.still_hard: Ensuring an informed, voluntary decision and responding to refusal, capacity concerns or changed preferences.
tasks.human_edge: The therapist can recognise hesitation and revisit an explanation instead of treating a signature as understanding.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated record entry; the consent conversation retains all time.

reach.task: Check whether the consent record identifies the actual intervention and decision

evidence.claim: Native forms may reduce repeated identity entry in consent documentation; meaningful consent remains a clinical conversation and patient decision.

assumptions: Boundary is obtaining and recording consent, excluding intervention execution and any separate capacity assessment.

Therapist produces the actual consent outcome in s1. In s2's 20 retained hours the therapist enters patient and encounter identifiers, intervention version, explanation topics, questions, decision, limits and date; current record identifiers are verified rather than captured again.

No structured consent flag is supplied free and no checkbox is preselected as agreement. Missing or conflicting information requires manual documentation and clarification; refusal blocks the intervention through existing clinical practice.
Test native forms before custom code. Existing prefills earn no new saving. Patient decision time is not counted as therapist saving, and local consent requirements remain to be confirmed.
unknowns: Current consent-documentation burden and native form fields
Local requirements and capacity escalation route
research_questions: Does the form reduce duplicate entry while preserving a specific, accurate record of explanation and voluntary decision?

already_counted.description: Consent discussion, explanation and understanding checks
Outcome capture and exact record checking

incremental.description: Maintain intervention fields and audit misleading consent entries

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=75+20=95; gross 5 minus 2 upkeep gives net 3. High requires repeated identity entry; low removes only 2 hours, offset by upkeep. The entire consent conversation remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Test patient function and record measurements

steps.what: Test and measure strength, development, function and relevant physiological capacity
Record patient test data, units, conditions and relevant limitations

tasks.design: Configure test-specific fields and unit checks in the clinical record {OTHER}, reusing the checked patient and encounter identifiers. The therapist performs every test and enters and verifies the actual measurement, conditions and limitations; no inferred result or unseen device feed is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated labels, units and encounter details can duplicate data-entry work after physical assessment.
tasks.enabler_now: Native structured forms can reduce repetitive entry and catch format errors.
tasks.still_hard: Obtaining valid measurements and recognising pain, fatigue, effort or contraindications that change interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: The therapist can stop a test or qualify a result when the patient's actual condition makes it unreliable.
tasks.altitude: Less repetitive record entry; physical testing and clinical observation keep their time.

reach.task: Interpret the recorded measurement conditions before reusing a functional result

evidence.claim: Native assessment forms can reduce repeated field entry while retaining measurement capture and checking; no measured physical-therapy saving is supplied.

assumptions: Boundary is physical assessment and data recording, excluding treatment evaluation and the wider encounter note.

Therapist produces all measurements in s1 with its full 80 hours retained. In s2's 13 retained hours the therapist captures patient, encounter, test, side, value, unit, date, conditions, assistance and limitations and checks them against the observation.

No ready structured measurement feed is assumed. Missing units, incompatible tests or uncertain observations require manual entry and clarification; format validation does not establish clinical validity.
Test native assessment forms first. Existing standard forms earn no new gain. No clinical conclusion is generated and no additional patient test is introduced.
unknowns: Current test mix, record forms and entry burden
Required units and local assessment protocols
research_questions: Do structured forms reduce total entry time without losing test conditions or introducing wrong-unit results?

already_counted.description: Measurement capture, unit checks and limitations entry

incremental.description: Maintain test fields, units and record-quality samples

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=80+13=93; gross 7 minus 2 upkeep gives net 5. High assumes repeated manual labels and identity entry; low removes only 2 hours, consumed by upkeep. Physical assessment retains all 80 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce narrow record-entry repetition while keeping treatment evaluation, informed consent, clinical coordination and physical assessment personal.
reach: Work with records specialists on specific consent records and therapists on comparable assessment data
role.ambitious_version: A therapist who records assessments clearly while preserving time for valid tests, patient understanding and treatment decisions.
